A LITTLE EXPERIMENT

Take your pendulum to the Moon.

Keep the length and release angle the same. Compare Earth and Moon gravity. Which world makes the pendulum take longer to complete one swing?

Inside this model +

The pendulum follows θ″ = −(g/L) sin θ − bθ′. Numerical integration uses fourth-order Runge–Kutta steps. Unlike the small-angle formula, the motion includes the full sin θ term.

The displayed period uses the chosen release angle: T = 4√(L/g) K(sin²(θ₀/2)), where K is the complete elliptic integral. It reduces to T = 2π√(L/g) for small angles. With damping enabled it is an undamped reference, not a measured damped period. The bob is treated as a point mass on a massless, rigid-length string.

Damping b is a simplified linear drag coefficient in s⁻¹. Changing a setting releases the pendulum again from the chosen angle. The graph shows its most recent 12 seconds, sampled during the integration so faster playback does not skip swings. Gravity values are representative, rounded values.
